comments.body:
RESEARCH — how actively-maintained Gerrit deployments configure outbound mail on AWS. Commissioned for this bug so the configure-vs-disable decision is grounded in real deployments and primary sources rather than invented. Every claim below carries a source; where nothing could be verified, that is stated explicitly rather than guessed.

# Gerrit outbound mail on AWS — grounded options

**Root cause confirmed against source.** Gerrit's `SmtpEmailSender` defaults `smtpServer` to `127.0.0.1` and, for `smtpEncryption = none|tls`, `smtpServerPort` to `25`. With no `[sendemail]` section at all, Gerrit dials `127.0.0.1:25` on every notification:

    smtpHost = cfg.getString("sendemail", null, "smtpserver");
    if (smtpHost == null) { smtpHost = "127.0.0.1"; }
    ...
    switch (smtpEncryption) {
      case SSL: defaultPort = 465; break;
      case NONE: case TLS: default: defaultPort = 25;
    }

— https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GerritCodeReview/gerrit/master/java/com/google/gerrit/server/mail/send/SmtpEmailSender.java

**Confirmed: the official image has no MTA, so `localhost:25` can never work.** `GerritCodeReview/docker-gerrit` `ubuntu/26/Dockerfile` installs only `gnupg2`, `sudo`, `openjdk-21-jdk` (then removes it), and `gerrit=3.14.1-1` on `eclipse-temurin` — no postfix/exim/ssmtp/msmtp/nullmailer, no `EXPOSE 25`. Its entrypoint writes exactly two config keys (`gerrit.canonicalWebUrl`, `httpd.listenUrl`) and the README documents exactly two env vars — no SMTP env vars at all.
— https://github.com/GerritCodeReview/docker-gerrit/blob/master/ubuntu/26/Dockerfile
— https://github.com/GerritCodeReview/docker-gerrit/blob/master/ubuntu/26/entrypoint.sh
— https://github.com/GerritCodeReview/docker-gerrit/blob/master/README.md

Note the official README's own production example contains `[sendemail] smtpServer = localhost`, which is misleading for a stock container — it only works if you supply an MTA yourself (see section 2).

## 1. Canonical `[sendemail]` keys

| Key | Accepted values / default | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `enable` | `true` (default). "If false Gerrit will not send email messages, for any reason, and all other properties of section sendemail are ignored." | config-gerrit; commit 2e4573b464 |
| `smtpServer` | hostname/IP; **default `127.0.0.1`** | SmtpEmailSender.java |
| `smtpServerPort` | default `25`, or `465` when `smtpEncryption = ssl` | SmtpEmailSender.java |
| `smtpEncryption` | **exactly `none` / `ssl` / `tls`** (enum; `tls` = STARTTLS). Default `none`. Typos like `tsl` silently fall through to the default — this bit a real reporter. | SmtpEmailSender.java; repo-discuss |
| `smtpUser` / `smtpPass` | optional; auth attempted **only if `smtpUser` is non-null** (`if (smtpUser != null && !client.auth(smtpUser, smtpPass))`) | SmtpEmailSender.java |
| `sslVerify` | default `true` | SmtpEmailSender.java |
| `from` | default `MIXED`; also `USER`, `SERVER`, or a literal `Name <addr>` with optional `${user}` placeholder | config-gerrit |
| `connectTimeout`, `includeDiff`, `threadPoolSize`, `allowrcpt`/`denyrcpt`, `threadIdPrefix` | see docs | config-gerrit |

— https://gerrit-review.googlesource.com/Documentation/config-gerrit.html#sendemail

**`smtpPass` belongs in `$site_path/etc/secure.config`, not `gerrit.config`.** `secure.config` "overrides or supplements the settings supplied by gerrit.config and should be readable only by the daemon process"; `gerrit init` actively moves `sendemail.smtpPass` into it. Optionally encryptable via the secure-config plugin + `gerrit passwd`.
— https://gerrit-review.googlesource.com/Documentation/config-gerrit.html
— https://gerrit.googlesource.com/plugins/secure-config/+/refs/heads/stable-2.13/README.md

**SES port/encryption matrix** (TLS is mandatory; there is no plaintext option):

| Mechanism | SES ports | Gerrit `smtpEncryption` |
|---|---|---|
| STARTTLS | 25, 587, 2587 | `tls` |
| TLS Wrapper (implicit SSL) | 465, 2465 | `ssl` |

— https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/dg/smtp-connect.html

## 2. How the big deployments actually do it

**Neither of the two largest public Gerrit instances uses a remote authenticated SMTP server. Both run a local MTA and set `smtpServer = localhost`.**

**OpenDev / OpenStack** — `playbooks/roles/gerrit/templates/gerrit.config.j2`:

    [sendemail]
        smtpServer = localhost
        from = MIXED
        includeDiff = false
        threadPoolSize = 4

Their Gerrit container also has no MTA. It works because the compose service runs `network_mode: host`, so `localhost:25` is the *host's* port 25, where the base exim role delivers direct via DNS (no smarthost, no auth). No `smtpUser`/`smtpPass`/`smtpEncryption` anywhere in the role.
— https://opendev.org/opendev/system-config/src/branch/master/playbooks/roles/gerrit/templates/gerrit.config.j2
— https://opendev.org/opendev/system-config/src/branch/master/playbooks/roles/gerrit/templates/docker-compose.yaml.j2
— https://opendev.org/opendev/system-config/src/branch/master/playbooks/roles/base/exim/README.rst

**Wikimedia** — `modules/gerrit/templates/gerrit.config.erb`:

    [sendemail]
        includeDiff = true
        connectTimeout = 30 sec
        smtpServer = localhost
        threadPoolSize = 2

Their `secure.config.erb` contains no `smtpPass` — again local MTA, unauthenticated.
— https://github.com/wikimedia/operations-puppet/blob/production/modules/gerrit/templates/gerrit.config.erb

**openfrontier/gerrit image** (the community image that does expose SMTP env vars). Note both behaviors relevant to us — it **disables email when no server is configured**, and routes the password to `secure.config`:

    if [ -z "${SMTP_SERVER}" ]; then
      set_gerrit_config sendemail.enable false
    else
      set_gerrit_config sendemail.enable true
      set_gerrit_config sendemail.smtpServer "${SMTP_SERVER}"
      [ -z "${SMTP_SERVER_PORT}" ] || set_gerrit_config sendemail.smtpServerPort "${SMTP_SERVER_PORT}"
      [ -z "${SMTP_USER}" ]        || set_gerrit_config sendemail.smtpUser "${SMTP_USER}"
      [ -z "${SMTP_PASS}" ]        || set_secure_config sendemail.smtpPass "${SMTP_PASS}"
      [ -z "${SMTP_ENCRYPTION}" ]  || set_gerrit_config sendemail.smtpEncryption "${SMTP_ENCRYPTION}"
    fi

— https://github.com/openfrontier/docker-gerrit/blob/master/gerrit-entrypoint.sh

**Explicitly NOT found** (stated rather than guessed):
- No public LF Releng / ONAP / O-RAN-SC Gerrit `sendemail` config. The only `org:lfit` hit is `lfit/korg-docs` `source/mail.rst`, which is `git send-email` *client* config for kernel.org — NOT a Gerrit server config. Do not cite it as one.
- `openstack-infra/puppet-gerrit` has been emptied; no puppet-era template retrieved.
- `GerritForge/docker-gerrit` is abandoned (CentOS 7.3, Gerrit 2.14) and documents no SMTP env vars.
- **No actively-maintained large Gerrit deployment was found publishing a `[sendemail]` block pointed at Amazon SES.** The SES config in Option A is assembled from documented Gerrit key names plus AWS SES docs — it is not copied from a production deployment.

## Option A — wire up SES

`etc/gerrit.config`:

    [sendemail]
        enable = true
        smtpServer = email-smtp.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
        smtpServerPort = 587
        smtpEncryption = tls
        smtpUser = AKIA................
        sslVerify = true
        connectTimeout = 30 sec
        from = MIXED

`etc/secure.config` (mode 0600, owned by the gerrit user):

    [sendemail]
        smtpPass = <SES SMTP password>

Restart Gerrit — `sendemail` is not hot-reloadable.

**SES prerequisites (each a hard blocker):**

1. **Sandbox is the #1 gotcha.** New accounts are in the SES sandbox **per Region**: send only to *verified* addresses, max 200 msgs/24h, 1 msg/sec. Reviewer notifications to arbitrary addresses are rejected until production access is granted (console, or `aws sesv2 put-account-details --production-access-enabled --mail-type TRANSACTIONAL`; first Support response ~24h). — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/dg/request-production-access.html
2. **Verify the sender identity in us-east-1.** Domain identity (Easy DKIM, 3 CNAMEs, up to 72h propagation) allows any address on the domain; an email identity covers one address. Identities are per-Region. Whatever lands in the `From` header must be covered. — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/dg/creating-identities.html
3. **SMTP credentials are NOT IAM access keys.** "Your SMTP credentials aren't identical to your AWS access keys." Generate via SES console -> SMTP settings -> Create SMTP credentials (creates an IAM user; password shown once). Per-Region. A documented HMAC-SHA256 derivation from an IAM secret key exists, with reference Python in the doc. — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/dg/smtp-credentials.html
4. **Port 25 is blocked on EC2 by default** — outbound port 25 to public IPv4/IPv6 is blocked. Use 587 (needs no support ticket). — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-resource-limits.html#port-25-throttle
5. **SMTP vs API.** Gerrit's sender is a plain SMTP client with no AWS SDK path, so the SES API is unreachable from Gerrit without an external relay. SMTP it is.

**IAM-role-based auth is NOT possible for SMTP** — directly relevant to our instance-role/SSM pattern:

> "Don't use temporary AWS credentials to derive SMTP credentials. The SES SMTP interface doesn't support SMTP credentials that have been generated from temporary security credentials."
> — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/dg/smtp-credentials.html

An EC2 instance profile yields exactly those temporary credentials, so the SMTP interface **requires a long-lived IAM user access key**. A VPC interface endpoint for SMTP exists (ports 465/587/2465/2587) but does not remove the username/password requirement, and is not supported in us-east-1 AZs `use1-az2`, `use1-az3`, `use1-az5`. — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/dg/send-email-set-up-vpc-endpoints.html

**On the SSM SecureString idea (ours):** viable and sensible, but note the limit. AWS's SES guide does not prescribe SSM/Secrets Manager for an app's SMTP password; the nearest AWS precedents are AMS storing SES SMTP credentials in Secrets Manager, and SES Mail Manager referencing relay creds by `secretARN`. Workable shape: keep the SMTP password in SSM SecureString, grant the instance role read access, materialize `etc/secure.config` at boot (same pattern as `ci-gerrit-ssh-key` / `g2p-github-pat`). That gets role-scoped *access to the secret*; the SMTP auth itself stays static. Rotation = new IAM access key + re-derive.

**Historical SES gotcha — now resolved.** An old thread reported SES rejecting Gerrit mail with `554 Transaction failed: Illegal header 'Mailing-List'`. No longer applies: current `MailHeader.java` has no `Mailing-List` header and all custom headers are `X-`-prefixed; SES also broadened header support in 2024.

## Option B — disable cleanly

This is a first-class, documented option, and precisely the scenario the flag was added for:

> "If false Gerrit will not send email messages, for any reason, and all other properties of section sendemail are ignored. By default, true, allowing notifications to be sent."
> "Some installations might be unable to connect to a SMTP relay, but are still useful through the web page UI, provided that reviewers check their dashboard periodically."
> — https://gerrit-review.googlesource.com/Documentation/config-gerrit.html#sendemail
> — https://opendev.org/opendev/gerrit/commit/2e4573b46409fc7481dbbf64b394bbc2e1ccff27

Config:

    [sendemail]
        enable = false

Restart Gerrit. Errors stop immediately — no other `sendemail` key is consulted.

**What is lost:**
- All notifications: review/comment/merge emails, `user-notify` watches, project watches, abandon/restore, and the review-bot's own mail. Reviewers must use the dashboard.
- **Self-service email registration/verification breaks.** Registering a new or secondary address sends a verification link; with mail off that flow fails (today it already fails with the same `EmailException`).
  - Documented admin workaround: `PUT /accounts/{id}/emails/{email}` with `no_confirmation: true`. "Only Gerrit administrators are allowed to add email addresses without confirmation." — https://gerrit-review.googlesource.com/Documentation/rest-api-accounts.html#create-email
- **Not affected:** git push/fetch, the review UI, SSH/HTTP API, CI integration, label voting, submit, replication, or inbound mail (`[receiveemail]` is a separate section).

## Recommendation

**Set `sendemail.enable = false` now; revisit SES only if a human ever needs out-of-band notification.**

1. It is the documented, upstream-intended remedy for exactly our situation — an installation that cannot reach an SMTP relay but is useful through the UI/API. One line, stops all 4,119 errors immediately, trivially reversible.
2. It matches how a mainstream Gerrit container already behaves: openfrontier's image sets `sendemail.enable false` automatically when no SMTP server is given.
3. The functional loss is scoped to notifications plus self-service email verification, and the latter has an official admin bypass (`no_confirmation`). For our bot-driven flow that is close to zero cost.
4. Option A is not a config change, it is a project: sandbox exit (AWS Support round-trip), domain verification with DNS + DKIM propagation up to 72h, and a long-lived IAM user access key that **cannot** be replaced by our instance role. That is a lot of standing credential surface for mail nobody reads.
5. Do not attempt to "fix" `localhost:25` in place — the official image demonstrably has no MTA.

**If mail is later needed**, two credible paths:
- **Direct to SES** — Option A config above, port 587 / `tls`. Simplest; couples Gerrit to a static SES credential.
- **Local relay -> SES** — host-side or sidecar Postfix/msmtp satellite with Gerrit at `smtpServer = localhost`. This is what both OpenDev and Wikimedia actually do (with direct-delivery exim rather than SES), and is the workaround the SES reporter on repo-discuss settled on after failing to connect Gerrit to SES directly. Requires `network_mode: host` or a compose sidecar since our container has no MTA. Buys queueing/retry and keeps the SES credential out of Gerrit's config; costs another moving part.
- A third-party (SendGrid/Mailgun) is configuration-identical from Gerrit's side and skips SES's sandbox and identity verification, at the cost of another vendor. No Gerrit-specific documentation was found for these — that is inference from the shared SMTP key set, not a citation.

compiled_state.description:
## Summary

Gerrit's outbound email has never worked on the production box
(`i-00880b2c7f13527c5`). `/var/gerrit/site/etc/gerrit.config` contains **no
`[sendemail]` section at all**, so Gerrit falls back to its built-in default SMTP
target of `localhost:25`. The official Gerrit container ships no MTA, nothing
listens on that port, and every outbound notification therefore fails.

This is the single largest error signature in the Gerrit logs by an order of
magnitude — **4,119 occurrences** across the retained history — and it is still
firing today.

## Reproduction Steps

1. SSM onto `i-00880b2c7f13527c5` (us-east-1).
2. `grep -A6 -iE '\[sendemail\]' /var/gerrit/site/etc/gerrit.config` — no
   `[sendemail]` section exists.
3. Comment on, merge, abandon, or push a new patchset to any Gerrit change.
4. `grep 'Cannot email' /var/gerrit/site/logs/error_log`.

## Expected vs Actual

- **Expected:** either outbound mail is configured and succeeds, or it is
  explicitly disabled (`sendemail.enable = false`) so Gerrit does not attempt it
  and does not log an error.
- **Actual:** Gerrit attempts SMTP on every notification and fails with
  `Connection refused`, emitting a multi-line ERROR + stack trace each time.

## Evidence

Counts over the retained Gerrit logs (`/var/gerrit/site/logs/error_log*`,
2026-06-30 → 2026-07-30):

```
Mail Error: Connection refused ....................... 4119
"Cannot email ..." error lines ....................... 3713
  ERROR EmailReviewComments : Cannot email comments for N,N ......... 2812
  ERROR EmailMerge : Cannot email merged notification for N .........  840
  ERROR EmailNewPatchSet : Cannot send email for new patch set N,N ..  385
  ERROR AbandonOp : Cannot email update for change N ................   40
in the CURRENT (live) error_log alone ................  135
```

Verbatim, most recent occurrences observed 2026-07-30:

```
[2026-07-30T20:49:16.668Z] [SendEmail-1[send-email merged]] ERROR
  com.google.gerrit.server.submit.EmailMerge : Cannot email merged notification
  for 1057 [CONTEXT SUBMISSION_ID="1057-1785444..."]
com.google.gerrit.exceptions.EmailException: Mail Error: Connection refused
    at com.google.gerrit.server.mail.send.SmtpEmailSender.open(SmtpEmailSender.java:457)

[2026-07-30T20:54:05.506Z] [SendEmail-1[send-email comments]] ERROR
  com.google.gerrit.server.change.EmailReviewComments : Cannot email comments
  for 1048,4 [CONTEXT SSH_SESSION="6e14303c" ...]
com.google.gerrit.exceptions.EmailException: Mail Error: Connection refused
    at com.google.gerrit.server.mail.send.SmtpEmailSender.open(SmtpEmailSender.java:457)
```

Daily spread (non-exhaustive sample of rotations) shows it is continuous, not a
burst: 06-30 → 2, 07-05 → 108, 07-10 → 230, 07-15 → 117, 07-20 → 17, 07-25 → 58,
07-28 → 56, 07-29 → 21, live log → 135.

## Why this was never caught

- No CloudWatch alarm covers Gerrit SMTP. The host probe publishes
  `voter_errors`, `deploy_errors`, `g2p_dispatch_errors`, `replication_errors`
  and `review_bot_merge_change_errors` to namespace `rebar/host`, but nothing
  counts email-send failures, so the `rebar-gerrit-*` alarm set stayed green
  throughout.
- The condition was noticed exactly once, in passing, and set aside without a
  ticket: a comment on story `9249` records "the gerrit log also carries a
  pre-existing SmtpEmailSender connect failure. That is unrelated to this story
  (no SMTP change here)". Correct in that narrow context, but no bug was filed.
- A search of all 1,584 tickets for `smtp` / `sendemail` / `Cannot email`
  returns that single `9249` comment and nothing else.

## Impact

- Reviewers and change owners receive **no** Gerrit notification of comments,
  merges, new patchsets, or abandons. Our flow is heavily bot-driven, so the
  functional impact may be small in practice — but that tradeoff has never been
  recorded as a decision anywhere.
- ~4,000 multi-line ERROR + stack-trace entries actively bury genuine errors in
  `error_log`, which measurably raised the cost of this very audit.
- Contrast with `c943`, where the decision *not* to ship voter logs to
  CloudWatch was deliberately recorded in `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md`.
  Here there is no configuration and no recorded decision — only silent failure.

## Decision required

Two legitimate resolutions; this bug should pick one explicitly rather than
leave the current silent-failure state:

- **(A) Wire up outbound mail** — configure `[sendemail]` against Amazon SES
  (secrets via SSM SecureString + the existing instance role, consistent with
  how `ci-gerrit-ssh-key` / `g2p-github-pat` are handled).
- **(B) Disable cleanly** — set `sendemail.enable = false` so Gerrit stops
  attempting delivery, and record the rationale in the runbook.

Research into how actively-maintained Gerrit deployments configure AWS mail is
attached as a comment on this ticket to ground that choice.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A decision between (A) configure SES and (B) disable cleanly is made and
      recorded in `infra/runbooks/` (not only in this ticket).
- [ ] `gerrit.config` carries an explicit `[sendemail]` section reflecting that
      decision; the config is materialized by the deploy path so it survives a
      compose-up and an autodeploy roll-forward.
- [ ] After the change, a fresh comment/merge/patchset on a Gerrit change
      produces **zero** `Cannot email` / `Mail Error: Connection refused` lines
      in `/var/gerrit/site/logs/error_log`.
- [ ] If (A): a test message is demonstrably delivered end-to-end, and the SES
      sandbox/production-access state is recorded.
- [ ] If (B): the lost functionality is enumerated in the runbook so the choice
      is reversible with full information.
- [ ] Observability gap closed: either the host probe counts email-send failures
      into `rebar/host` with an alarm, or the runbook states why not (mirroring
      the `c943` precedent).
- [ ] File paths: `infra/gerrit/` (gerrit.config materialization),
      `infra/scripts/observability.sh`, `infra/runbooks/`.

file_impact.reason: add email-send failure counter to rebar/host metrics
